BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dil OILG OPINION NO. FEB 05 2025 HON. LUZVIMINDA A. LABAO Municipal Mayor Municipality of Mambusao Province of Capiz Dear Mayor Labao: This has reference to your letter dated 14 August 2024 seeking this Department's legal opinion and guidance regarding the validity of Municipal Appropriation Ordinance, ratifying the proposed borrowing of the municipality issued by the Sangguniang Bayan of Mambusao, Capiz, viz: I. Whether the Appropriations Ordinance is deemed approved due to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan's inaction within the 30-day period; and 2. Whether the Appropriation Ordinance was valid due to the affirmation of the SP of Capiz; Per the representation, the LGU of Mambusao passed the Municipal Appropriation Ordinance No. 3, series of 2024 on April 4, 2023, ratifying the proposed borrowing of the municipality. You represented that said ordinance was then submitted to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Capiz for review and validation on the same day. You then mentioned that on June 18, 2024, the SP of Capiz issued Resolution No. 857, series of 2024, unanimously approved the Sangguniang Bayan of Mambusao's Municipal Appropriation Ordinance No. 3, ratifying the proposed borrowing of the municipality. Finally, you represented that on July 1, 2024, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Capiz issued Resolution No. 878, series of 2024 recalling the previously issued Resolution approving the appropriations ordinance, dated June 18, 2024. However, you represented that the municipality has already secured the certificate of Net Debt Service Ceiling and Borrowing Capacity from the Department of Finance, Bureau of Local Government Finance (BLGF) which upholds the municipality's capacity to pay for the said loan. Thus, the request for legal opinion. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Before dwelling to your queries, allow us first to quote the specific provisions of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) which is pertinent to your queries: "Section 327. Review of Appropriation Ordinances of Component Cities and Municipalities. - The sangguniang panlalawigan shall review the ordinance authorizing annual or supplemental appropriations of component cities and municipalities in the same manner and within the same period prescribed for the review of other ordinances. If within ninety (90) days from receipt of copies of such ordinance. the sangqunianq panlalawigan takes no action thereon. the same shall be deemed to have been reviewed in accordance with law and shall continue to be in full force and effect. If within the same period, the sangguniang panlalawigan shall have ascertained that the ordinance authorizing annual or supplemental appropriations has not complied with the requirements set forth in this Title, the sangguniang panlalawigan shall, within the ninety-day period hereinabove prescribed declare such ordinance inoperative in its entirety or in part. Items of appropriation contrary to limitations prescribed in this Title or in excess of the amounts prescribed herein shall be disallowed or reduced accordingly. The sangguniang panlalawigan shall within the same period advise the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned through the local chief executive of any action on the ordinance under review. Upon receipt of such advice, the city or municipal treasurer concerned shall not make further disbursements of funds from any of the items of appropriation declared inoperative, disallowed or reduced." Section 320. Effectivity of Budgets. - The ordinance enacting the annual budget shall take effect at the beginning of the ensuing calendar year. An ordinance enacting a supplemental budget, however, shall take effect upon its approval or on the date fixed therein. The responsibility for the execution of the annual and supplemental budgets and the accountability therefor shall be vested primarily in the local chief executive concerned." Coming now to the first query, we answer in the negative. Section 327 of the Code is unambiguous in providing the 90-day period within which the Sangguniang Panlalawigan must review appropriations ordinance of component cities and municipalities commences from the date of receipt by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of the copies of such ordinance.l If no action has been taken by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan within the said 90-day period as reckoned from the date of receipt of the appropriations ordinance, the same DILG opinion No. 19, S. 2011, May 27, 2011 Page 2 of 4

shall be deemed to have been reviewed in accordance with law and shall continue to be in full force and effect. Thus, the inaction of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan within 30 days does not render the Appropriation Ordinance deemed approved. The contention that the Appropriation Ordinance is deemed approved due to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan's inaction within the 30-day period is legally erroneous considering that review of appropriation measure is governed by the 90-day period under Section 327 of the LGC. As to the this Department has consistently opined that since the subject ordinance in question have already been reviewed and approved, the same should be accorded the presumption of validity unless the courts of justice rule otherwise. Based on the records, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Capiz has already reviewed and upheld the Appropriation Ordinance on June 1 8, 2024, through Resolution No. 857, series of 2024, which effectively allowed the Municipality of Mambusao to borrow Php 100,000,000.00 from the Development Bank of the Philippines to finance the concreting of various farm-to-market roads. Upon ratification and approval of the said Ordinance, it immediately became valid and effective. The subsequent Resolution No. 878, Series of 2024, recalling Resolution No. 857 did not render the Appropriation Ordinance invalid. In other words, Resolution No. 857 cannot be recalled because it would create a situation in which ordinances already reviewed and upheld by the SP would become dependent on the will of the reviewing Sanggunian via a recall Resolution. Hence, the subject Appropriation Ordinance is accorded presumption of validity. Unless invalidity or unreasonableness is ostensibly apparent, one seeking a judicial declaration of the invalidity of an ordinance is duty-bound to adduce evidence that is convincingly indicative of its infirmities or defects.2 Until after the judiciary, in appropriate case, declare its invalidity, it is entitled to obedience and respect.3 The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, ATTY. ROMEO .
